A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LGKDE research and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–G. Content can be matched across the reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original synthetic graph experiments, anomaly-detection benchmarks, ablations, contamination studies, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical results and adds dataset evaluations, perturbation and capacity controls, distribution-shift experiments, and runtime analyses.

M1.justification: The GNN embeddings, MMD metric, feature and spectral perturbations, learnable KDE mixture, density-contrast objective, and inference procedures remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–3 and the reference-sampling strategies match across versions.

E1.justification: Appendix B.4 adds Mutagenicity, NCI109, FRANKENSTEIN, and Tox21AhR evaluations, described as spanning molecular, toxicological, and synthetic domains. Appendix B.7 adds sparse and dense shifts in normal ER graph distributions. The original twelve benchmarks and synthetic graph families remain.

E2.justification: The original accuracy comparisons and two-stage KDE comparator sets are retained. However, CVTGAD is removed from the COLLAB runtime comparison when v3 Table 12 becomes v4 Table 18. ARMET is newly discussed but is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: New protocols include perturbation-threshold grids, GNN widths of 32–256 and depths of 1–5 crossed with three KDE configurations, and ER shift tests using 2,000 training graphs and 500 normal plus 500 anomalous test graphs per scenario. Runtime analysis adds twelve node-count bins with fifty sampled pairs each.

E4.justification: v4 adds feature-only, spectral-only, and random-edge perturbation controls; threshold sensitivity and edge-change measurements; KDE-versus-GNN-capacity controls; controlled distribution shifts; and MMD timing versus graph size. These extend the retained component, depth, bandwidth, and contamination analyses rather than merely redisplaying them.

E5.justification: Five-seed benchmark reporting remains. Runtime reporting changes from explicitly ten-run training/inference uncertainties to total-time uncertainties with the count described only as repeated runs. New Figure 13 specifies standard deviations over fifty graph pairs and a least-squares timing fit; this does not establish increased benchmark run counts.

E6.justification: Matched benchmark and validation tables retain their numerical values. v4 adds substantial dataset, ablation, shift, and timing results; Table 15 reports mean AUROC degradation of 6.16 points for LGKDE versus 15.69 for OCGIN and 15.81 for SIGNET. Separate training/inference timings are removed. New Table 9 labels the default ENZYMES score 52.79 as AUROC, conflicting with retained Table 1's 71.04; this is not an established same-setting performance decline.

T1.justification: Theorems 4.1–4.6, assumptions, complexity results, and proofs are retained. v3 Appendix F.3 already contains the scalar-distance, h^-1 variance argument for intrinsic dimension one. v4 F.3.1 expands that explanation, while Theorem F.6 restates the existing generalization bound.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same density-estimation framework, theoretical guarantees, and anomaly-detection claims. The expanded title makes an already central application explicit; the additional experiments support existing contributions.

C2.justification: v4 substantially expands explanations of complementary feature/spectral perturbations, adaptive KDE benefits beyond parameter count, shift robustness through the learned density landscape, and practical amortization of quadratic MMD costs by GPU parallelism. The earlier limitations concerning massive graph collections and unsupported graph modalities remain.

D1.justification: v4 adds an explicit LGKDE repository link in place of the future-release statement and removes Listing 1. It also removes the dedicated training-details subsection, including the 500-epoch maximum and patience of ten. Most architecture, optimizer, hardware, and baseline settings remain. The PDFs establish the access pointer, not external repository availability.

R1.justification: New Appendix C.2 develops detailed positioning against flows, VAEs, and energy-based models, and explains LGKDE's relationship to Sun and Fan's existing deep MMD framework and its choice of two-stage comparisons. ARMET discussion and intrinsic-dimension references further extend the earlier related-work treatment.

P1.justification: The title, affiliations, publication text, and selected paragraphs are revised; acknowledgements, an impact statement, and explanatory subsections are added. The principal section sequence and much of the abstract, methodology, and conclusion remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references adopt a two-column layout. The old component-ablation table and vertically stacked plots move into the main text as Table 2 and horizontally arranged Figure 5. New tables and Figure 13 are added, and the runtime table is rebuilt around datasets and total times.

improvement.justification: The added perturbation and capacity controls strengthen evidence for the existing design claims, while distribution-shift and runtime tests broaden practical validation. These gains are tempered by removed training details and the new ENZYMES AUROC inconsistency between Tables 9 and 1. The revision provides a limited net quality improvement rather than resolving the paper's broader methodological and theoretical limitations.
